messages.subject: Aligning legend labels
parts:
Occasionally I plot classified data, i.e. factors that correspond to
numeric ranges. Those numeric ranges I need to present on a legend,
e.g.

1 - 5
6 - 10
11 - 50
51 - 100
101 -

Is there any way to have those those dashes and both numbers line up
nicely? I have been using zero padding, but that's a bit ugly.

001 - 005
006 - 010
011 - 050
051 - 100
101 -

I have tried using unicode figure spaces for padding, but those don't
survive to pdf output.

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Aligning legend labels
parts:
You could use phantom, but it's a bit of a pain to set up,

labs <- paste(c(1,10, 100, 1000), "-", c(1,10, 100, 1000), sep="")

d <- data.frame(x=rnorm(100), f=rep(labs, each=25))

foo <- function(l, pad.max=4){

sp <- strsplit(l, "-")[[1]]

l1 <- nchar(sp[1])
l2 <- nchar(sp[2])
ph1 <- paste(rep("0", length= pad.max - l1), collapse="")
ph2 <- paste(rep("0", length= pad.max - l2), collapse="")
as.expression(bquote(phantom(.(ph1)) * .(sp[1]) ~ "-" ~
phantom(.(ph2))*.(sp[2])))

}

qplot(x, x, color=f, data=d) +
scale_colour_discrete(breaks = labs, labels = llply(labs, foo))

HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: Aligning legend labels
parts:
On 6.4.2011 13:16, baptiste auguie wrote:
> You could use phantom, but it's a bit of a pain to set up,

Thanks. It works great. For anyone interested, the function I adapted
to suit my usual needs from Baptiste's code is below. It takes two
vectors -- the lower and upper bounds of ranges and optionally a
separator, which defaults to an en dash. Works for well non-integers too
as long as you format the bounds with sprintf to an equal amount of
decimals prior to calling.

range.labels = function(a, b, sep="\u2013")
{
na = max(nchar(a)) - nchar(a)
nb = max(nchar(b)) - nchar(b)
a0 = sapply(na, function(x) paste(rep("0", x), collapse=""))
b0 = sapply(nb, function(x) paste(rep("0", x), collapse=""))
labels = sapply(seq_along(a), function(i) {
as.expression(bquote(phantom(.(a0[i])) * .(a[i]) ~ .(sep) ~
phantom(.(b0[i])) * .(b[i])))

})
return(labels)
}
